papers.title: Sleep pressure is increased by protein fragments and decreased by processive proteolysis.
papers.abstract: Sleep is universal among animals, yet the molecular-level causes and functions of sleep are incompletely understood. The fragment generation hypothesis (FGH) posits that sleep, at least in part, is an adaptive response to protein fragments, many of them protein-sized, that accumulate during wakefulness owing to cleavages by proteases, including caspases and Ca2+-activated calpains. According to the FGH, these fragments are a source of homeostatic sleep pressure that increases during wakefulness, and one function of sleep is to decrease protein fragment levels through their slower production and faster degradation during sleep. Predictions of the FGH have not previously been tested. Using zebrafish, we show that pharmacological inhibition of caspases decreases sleep, in agreement with the prediction of the FGH that a slower production of protein fragments would decrease sleep pressure. Pharmacological inhibition of the proteasome is shown to have the opposite effect, an increased sleep, in agreement with another prediction of the FGH, that sleep pressure would increase if fragments are protected from their proteasome-mediated degradation. Consistent with this prediction, a caspase-generated subunit of the activated caspase-3 is strongly upregulated by a sleep-increasing inhibition of the proteasome. The increase of sleep by proteasome inhibitors was found to be reduced by inhibition of calpains, suggesting that calpain-generated, proteasome-degradable protein fragments contribute to sleep pressure. Pharmacological inhibition of calpains also causes a decrease in rebound sleep after sleep deprivation, as predicted by the FGH. Together, these results suggest that the FGH may provide a molecular-level explanation of a cause and function of sleep.

papers.title: NED-Net: open-source software for building and refining seizure detectors during rodent EEG experiments
papers.abstract: Long-term EEG is the main readout of rodent epilepsy models, and automated detectors are usually delivered as fixed models that a laboratory cannot adapt to its own animals. NED-Net is open-source software in which annotations, rule-based detections and model proposals share one file per recording, reviewed events train the next detector, and detection runs live during acquisition, so a detector can be refined while an experiment runs. A detector built in NED-Net on one kainate mouse cohort detected 64% of 221 video-adjudicated convulsive seizures in a second cohort as delivered, and 72% of its detections on held-out recordings were seizures. Retraining on annotations made in the app, a few seconds of review per event, raised recall to 88% at 74% precision. SeizyML, a published detector, reached similar recall with three times the detections and did not improve with the same annotations. A convulsive classifier removes non-seizures and enriches convulsive events.

papers.title: LogicSleep: a neurosymbolic-guided framework for explainable and personalized sleep staging.
papers.abstract: Sleep staging is important for diagnosing and managing sleep disorders. However, artificial intelligence-based models still struggle with explainability, sequence plausibility, and personalization across subjects. We propose LogicSleep, a neurosymbolic framework that integrates transition rules with deep learning models for explainable, physiologically valid, and subject-adaptive sleep staging. LogicSleep extracts multi-level evidence from raw polysomnography via a CNN-graph U-Net backbone, providing explainable patterns beyond classification. Sequence plausibility is enforced by combining Conditional Random Fields with Deep Learning with Differentiable Logics (DL2) rules, which discourage implausible transitions, promote physiologically valid ones, and regularize dwell times; the same rules also guide subject-specific test-time adaptation via entropy minimization. Across different datasets (i.e., ISRUC_S1, ISRUC_S3, and MASS_SS3 datasets), under both within- and cross-dataset settings, LogicSleep consistently outperforms strong baselines and improves sequence-level metrics. Ablations confirm complementary contributions of each component. LogicSleep advances sleep staging toward physiologically plausible, personalized, and explainable predictions.

papers.title: The insular cortex and arousal: insights from a human focal lesion-based model.
papers.abstract: Wakefulness depends on distributed cortico-subcortical networks integrating arousal and cognitive processes. Although the insular cortex is not traditionally considered a core component of sleep-wake regulation, its connectivity suggests a modulatory role in humans. We retrospectively investigated patients with insular gliomas undergoing awake craniotomy with intraoperative neurophysiological and neuropsychological monitoring. We identified patients exhibiting transient episodes of impaired task engagement and responsiveness during active intraoperative testing, defined as the intra-surgical falling asleep phenomenon (ISFAP) based primarily on behavioral and task-related criteria. Associated electroencephalographic (EEG) and electrocorticographic (ECoG) features were subsequently characterized as supportive neurophysiological correlates. These patients were compared with matched controls who did not develop ISFAP. Forty-six patients were included (22 ISFAP; 24 controls). ISFAP was associated with neurophysiological patterns resembling non-rapid eye movement sleep, including theta-delta slow waves and spindle-like oscillatory activity. In univariate analyses, ISFAP was more frequent in right-sided insular tumors and patients receiving train-of-five stimulation, although these associations were not retained in multivariable models. Within the ISFAP group, inability to resume task performance after episode onset was associated with left-sided lesions. ISFAP is a transient behavioral phenomenon accompanied by sleep-like neurophysiological features during cognitive engagement in a subset of patients undergoing awake surgery for insular gliomas. These findings raise the hypothesis of transient arousal instability in the context of lesion-related network dysfunction, potentially influenced by the awake-surgery setting. Recognition of ISFAP may improve the interpretation of neuropsychological performance during awake surgery.

Right-sided tumors and train-of-five stimulation were associated with ISFAP in univariate but not multivariable analyses, suggesting transient arousal instability from lesion-related network dysfunction.

papers.title: Spectral and complexity-based signatures of advanced concentration absorption meditation: A high-density EEG study of jhana
papers.abstract: Advanced meditation provides structured and reproducible alterations of consciousness that are increasingly used as model states for the neuroscience of consciousness. Jhana-type advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J) consists of eight progressively deepening absorption states (ACAM-J1-8) in which sensory and self-referential content gradually attenuate. We applied high-density EEG and a comprehensive multidimensional battery of spectral and complexity measures to characterize each ACAM-J state individually in 20 advanced meditators, together with phenomenological ratings. ACAM-J produced widespread posterior-central reductions in oscillatory and aperiodic power, posterior aperiodic flattening across all eight states, and convergent increases in entropy-based complexity over the posterior cortex, with power effects strengthening with phenomenological depth. Crucially, neural complexity remained elevated even in the late, most minimal and unified states, in opposition to the prevailing account that links higher neural entropy to richer phenomenal content. Between practitioners, lower power and higher entropy accompanied more visual and auditory but less bodily content, a redistribution rather than an enrichment of experience; within practitioners, only reduced low-frequency power tracked wider attention and less narrative thought. ACAM-J thus emerges as a non-pharmacological model state at the high-complexity end of the spectrum of altered consciousness, and reveals a previously unquantified dissociation between neural complexity and experiential richness for specific ACAM-J states.

papers.title: The chronobiology of brain waste clearance: Sleep-wake and circadian regulation of glymphatic function.
papers.abstract: The glymphatic system - a glia-dependent perivascular network mediating cerebrospinal fluid and interstitial fluid exchange - has emerged as a key determinant of restorative sleep, with its efficiency governed by both sleep-wake state and the circadian clock. Its activity peaks during NREM slow-wave sleep and is essential for clearing neurotoxic proteins including amyloid-β and hyperphosphorylated tau, whose accumulation underlies Alzheimer's disease and related neurodegenerative proteinopathies. This activity is itself under circadian control, with aquaporin-4 expression, CSF production, and perivascular flow exhibiting diurnal rhythmicity driven by the suprachiasmatic clock and peripheral clock genes. Recent work identifying synchronized norepinephrine oscillations from the locus coeruleus as the primary driver of glymphatic vasomotion has reframed the system's mechanistic architecture and raised questions about sedative-hypnotics and circadian disruption, both of which suppress this oscillatory pattern. This review synthesizes mechanistic, biomarker, and therapeutic evidence into a chronobiological framework positioning glymphatic efficiency as a distinct dimension of sleep quality - one that conventional EEG-based staging fails to capture. We examine disruption of glymphatic function by circadian misalignment, aging, sleep fragmentation, and neurodegeneration, and evaluate emerging biomarkers - including DTI-ALPS and plasma markers of waste accumulation - appraising their validity and limitations. Drawing on a broad literature survey and publication-trend analysis, we identify emerging perspectives to inform targeted therapeutic strategies. The therapeutic landscape is assessed across non-pharmacological, chronotherapeutic, pharmacological, and vascular and meningeal lymphatic interventions. We identify a translational gap between preclinical and human evidence, and propose that glymphatic biomarker endpoints be incorporated into sleep and chronobiology trials as a scientific priority.

papers.title: Sleep-Deprivation Serum Induces Mitochondrial Stress in BV2 Cells: Responses to P2Y12-Targeted Pharmacological Modulation.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) disrupts neuroimmune and metabolic homeostasis, but whether circulating factors generated after sleep loss alter microglial responses to purinergic pharmacological modulation remains unclear. P2Y12 is a microglia-enriched purinergic receptor that regulates process dynamics, calcium signaling, and microglial interactions with neurons and vascular-glial interfaces. Here, we established an in vitro serum-transfer model to test whether serum from sleep-deprived mice alters mitochondrial and Rhod-2 fluorescence responses to P2Y12-targeted compounds in BV2 cells. Mice were subjected to forced-wheel SD consisting of one wheel revolution every 2 s for 4 h per day over 4 consecutive days, and serum was obtained by cardiac blood collection followed by centrifugation. BV2 cells were treated with control or SD serum in the absence or presence of the P2Y12 antagonist MRS2395 or the P2Y12 agonist 2-MeSADP. Mitochondrial membrane potential was assessed by JC-1 red/green ratio imaging, mitochondrial network integrity by MitoTracker-based segmentation and skeletonization, and Rhod-2 fluorescence responses by single-cell F/F0 imaging. SD serum decreased the JC-1 ratio, increased maximal depolarization, reduced mitochondrial skeleton length and mitochondrial area fraction, and suppressed Rhod-2 responses. Under control-serum conditions, MRS2395 markedly enhanced Rhod-2 responses, whereas the increase in the area under the Rhod-2 response curve with 2-MeSADP was not significant after Holm correction. Under SD-serum conditions, however, neither compound consistently restored the mitochondrial or Rhod-2 response profile. Together, these findings link SD-serum exposure to mitochondrial impairment and attenuated Rhod-2 fluorescence responses in BV2 cells, and suggest that serum context may influence cellular responses to P2Y12-targeted compounds.

papers.title: Psychedelics and Sleep: Preclinical and Human Studies-A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Background: Classic psychedelics, including LSD, psilocybin, and N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT)/ayahuasca, have shown promise as rapid-acting treatments for psychiatric disorders. Because sleep plays a central role in emotional regulation and neuroplasticity, psychedelic-induced changes in sleep architecture are of interest. Methods: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. PubMed was searched for preclinical and clinical studies published up to May 1, 2026, investigating psychedelics and sleep-related outcomes. Twelve eligible studies evaluated LSD, psilocybin, or DMT/ayahuasca and assessed sleep architecture, sleep quality, electroencephalographic activity, or dreams. Study validity was assessed using appropriate methodological tools. Results: Preclinical studies consistently demonstrated acute REM sleep suppression, delayed REM onset, increased wakefulness, and transient disruption of non-REM sleep. Human findings were more heterogeneous, although randomized trials reported prolonged REM latency after psilocybin and reduced REM duration after ayahuasca. Evidence regarding slow-wave activity (SWA) was mixed, with ayahuasca increasing early-cycle SWA and psilocybin reducing absolute delta power during the first sleep cycle. Subjective sleep quality showed little acute change in controlled trials, whereas one large naturalistic study reported reductions in sleep disturbances following psilocybin. Administration close to bedtime appeared more disruptive than daytime dosing. In general, quality assessments indicated fair-to-poor validity and notable risk of bias. Conclusions: Classic psychedelics produce acute but transient alterations in sleep physiology, particularly affecting REM sleep. Whether these changes contribute to therapeutic effects remains uncertain. Larger, well-controlled studies using standardized polysomnographic methods are needed to clarify the relationship between psychedelic-induced sleep modulation and clinical outcomes. This review was not prospectively registered.

Evidence on slow-wave activity was mixed, and included studies showed fair-to-poor validity and notable risk of bias.

papers.title: Data-Driven EEG-fMRI Fusion: From Multimodal Integration to Latent Neural Inference.
papers.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) capture neural dynamics across complementary temporal and spatial scales, but analyzing them jointly is difficult: the two modalities differ in measurement mechanisms, temporal resolution, and neurovascular coupling. EEG-fMRI fusion can be framed as an inverse problem, where the goal is to recover latent neural processes only partially observed through electrophysiological and hemodynamic signals. Here, we review data-driven fusion methods published between 2000 and 2025, focusing on techniques that identify shared neural representations across modalities. We organize methods by fusion strategies (symmetric vs. asymmetric), methodological objectives (factorization vs. translation), and modeling assumptions (linear vs. nonlinear), and discuss evaluation metrics and visualization strategies in current use. A recurring finding is the absence of a universal validation standard and the difficulty of interpreting latent multimodal components. Across neurological, psychiatric, and cognitive applications, EEG-fMRI fusion has revealed distributed network dynamics not accessible through unimodal analyses, though temporal misalignment, noise-induced coupling, and model-dependent interpretation remain persistent challenges. We close by discussing directions including nonlinear modeling, flexible coupling frameworks, and large-scale group-level fusion, and situate the field within a broader view of EEG-fMRI fusion as a problem of latent neural inference.

papers.title: Brainstem Circuits Engaged During REM Sleep Regulate Apnea Susceptibility.
papers.abstract: Breathing is dynamically regulated across sleep-wake states. However, how brainstem circuits support respiratory output during sleep, particularly during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, remains unclear. Here, we show that neurons in the preBötzinger Complex (preBötC), a core inspiratory rhythm generator, selectively exhibit elevated calcium activity during REM sleep. Inhibition of these neurons selectively increases apnea occurrence during REM sleep. Optogenetic activation produces state-dependent effects, inducing prolonged apnea during REM sleep and increasing the breathing rate during wakefulness. We further identify an upstream lateral parabrachial nucleus (LPBN) projection to the preBötC that showed related state-dependent effects. Inhibition of these preBötC-projecting LPBN neurons increases apnea susceptibility during REM sleep, whereas activation induces prolonged apnea during REM sleep. Together, our findings identify REM-engaged preBötC neurons and LPBN-preBötC projection-defined neurons, whose perturbation preferentially disrupts breathing during REM sleep. This state-dependent vulnerability may provide insights into the mechanisms that contribute to sleep-related respiratory disorders.

papers.title: From real to synthetic: PSG-GAN learns sleep apnea signal dynamics for AI training
papers.abstract: Synthetic polysomnography (PSG) data has great potential in healthcare applications, for example in substituting real data that is sensitive and challenging to collect. Previous research on synthetic PSG data has been largely focused on short segments of individual signals, overlooking the inter-signal dynamics related to sleep disorders. In this study, we developed a generative adversarial network (PSG-GAN) for co-synthesizing longer segments of multiple PSG signals with diverse and complex characteristics typical of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). The synthetic signals appeared realistic, and the electroencephalography and electrooculography band powers were similarly distributed across sleep stages. Moreover, the PSG-GAN learned to mirror signal interactions such as changes in photoplethysmography-based heart rate during and after breathing obstructions. An automatic scoring model trained solely with automatically scored synthetic signals reached good performance on sleep staging (\k{appa}=0.71 and 0.63) and respiratory event segmentation (\k{appa}=0.57 and 0.60), on two test sets consisting of healthy volunteers and OSA patients, respectively. This demonstrates the potential of synthetic data in supporting algorithm development for sleep diagnostics. The source code is available at https://github.com/rikuhuttunen/psg-gan.

papers.title: Circadian modulation of dopamine release shapes reward-evoked signaling in the nucleus accumbens.
papers.abstract: The circadian system is an important regulator of reward-related neural function and behavior. Dopamine (DA) release in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) is a key component of reward processing, yet how circadian timing shapes DA release in relation to reward behavior remains unclear. Here, we investigated circadian rhythms in DA release and reward behavior in C57BL/6J mice expressing the genetically encoded DA sensor DA3m in the NAc using long-term fiber photometry paired with an automated reward delivery and measurement system. Spontaneous DA, reflecting broad changes in DA release during natural behavior, peaked during the early subjective day. In a separate group of mice, targeted disruption of the molecular clock gene Bmal1 in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) strongly attenuated spontaneous DA rhythmicity, supporting a role for the SCN molecular clock in regulating these rhythms. Reward-evoked DA peaked during the day-to-night transition, while cue-evoked DA and reward behavior peaked during the early subjective night. Linear mixed-effects modeling showed that reward-evoked DA was positively associated with reward behavior and cue-evoked DA but negatively associated with baseline DA measured immediately before reward availability. Reward-evoked DA differed across circadian time even after accounting for reward behavior or cue-evoked DA, while higher baseline DA predicted smaller reward-evoked responses and the strength of this relationship also changed across circadian time. Together, these findings show that circadian time changes both the magnitude of reward-evoked DA responses and how those responses relate to baseline and cue-evoked dopamine signaling and reward behavior.

SCN-specific Bmal1 disruption attenuated spontaneous dopamine rhythmicity, and reward-evoked dopamine was positively associated with reward behavior and cue-evoked dopamine but negatively associated with pre-reward baseline dopamine.

papers.title: Regular physical activity and a 12-week structured exercise program: Associations with circadian organization and sleep in permanent night-shift workers.
papers.abstract: Permanent night-shift work induces circadian misalignment, sleep disruption, and impaired physiological organization. Although exercise is increasingly recognized as a non-photic zeitgeber, its long-term association with circadian adaptation under occupational conditions remains poorly understood. To examine whether habitual physical activity and a 12-week supervised exercise program are associated with circadian organization, sleep, and physiological rhythms in permanent night-shift workers. Study 1 was a cross-sectional comparison of 12 habitually physically active and 12 sedentary permanent night-shift workers matched for major demographic and occupational characteristics. Study 2 was an uncontrolled longitudinal before-after intervention in 16 initially sedentary workers. Using the same ambulatory protocol, activity-rest rhythms, oral temperature, sleep, and neuromuscular, respiratory, cardiovascular, and cognitive variables were repeatedly assessed across an entire work-rest cycle. Habitually physically active workers exhibited greater rhythm amplitude, dominant oscillatory periods closer to 24 h during the workweek, higher sleep efficiency, and more coherent temporal organization across several physiological systems than sedentary workers. Similar pre-to-post changes were observed in Study 2. During weekend recovery, dominant oscillatory periods transiently shortened to approximately 18-22 h, concurrently with rapid repositioning of activity-rest and oral-temperature acrophases toward diurnal timing. These dynamics most likely reflect adaptive circadian reorganization rather than changes in endogenous circadian period. Regular physical activity was associated with greater circadian robustness, temporal coherence, and better sleep. Because Study 2 lacked a control group, the longitudinal changes cannot be attributed exclusively to the exercise program. Controlled studies using direct phase markers are required.

papers.title: Influence of social housing on dim light at night induced behavioural and hepatic alterations in mice.
papers.abstract: Circadian disruption induced by dim light at night (DLAN) is increasingly recognised as an environmental stressor that adversely affects behavioural and metabolic physiology. While social interaction is known to buffer stress responses, whether it mitigates DLAN-induced behavioural and hepatic dysfunction remains poorly understood. Therefore, this study investigated the influence of social housing on behavioural, oxidative and hepatic alterations induced by chronic DLAN exposure in male mice. Sixty-four mice were assigned to four experimental groups comprising group-housed and socially isolated animals maintained under either a standard light-dark cycle or DLAN for 28 days. Behavioural assessments were performed to evaluate anxiety-like behaviour and anhedonia, followed by histological examination of the liver and biochemical analyses of antioxidant enzyme activities, glucose and hepatic function biomarkers. DLAN exposure increased anxiety-like behaviour, anhedonia, oxidative stress and hepatic dysfunction, with these effects being most pronounced in socially isolated mice. Histological analyses revealed marked hepatocellular degeneration and lipid accumulation in isolated DLAN-exposed animals, accompanied by reduced catalase and superoxide dismutase activities and elevated glucose, triglyceride and hepatic enzyme levels. In contrast, group-housed mice exposed to DLAN exhibited significantly attenuated behavioural deficits, improved antioxidant status and reduced hepatic injury compared with their socially isolated counterparts. These findings demonstrate that social housing alleviates DLAN-induced behavioural and hepatic dysfunction, highlighting the importance of social interaction as a modulator of physiological resilience during circadian disruption.

papers.title: Intranasal dexmedetomidine sedation in pediatric electroencephalography: dose optimization, safety, and EEG characteristics.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of intranasal dexmedetomidine (DEX) for sedation during pediatric EEG and to explore whether EEG spectral characteristics under DEX differ from those under chloral hydrate. In this retrospective cohort study, 224 children (0-18 years) who underwent EEG under intranasal DEX sedation at a single tertiary center (January 2024-April 2025) were analyzed. Patients were stratified into weight-based dosing (Group 1, <50 kg; median 2 μg/kg) and fixed dosing (Group 2, ≥50 kg; median 100 μg). Sedation success, onset time, total sedation time, and adverse events were assessed. In a within-subject subgroup of 11 patients with a prior chloral hydrate EEG, relative power spectral density (rPSD) in the delta, theta, alpha, and beta bands during N1 and N2 sleep was compared using patient-level paired analyses, with mean paired differences, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and correction for multiple comparisons. Initial sedation success was 94.6% in Group 1 and 94.7% in Group 2; all patients achieved adequate sedation after rescue dosing. Median onset time was 10 minutes in both groups. Adverse events were mild and self-limited (3.2% and 2.6%). No statistically significant differences in rPSD between DEX and chloral hydrate were detected in either sleep stage after correction for multiple comparisons; however, the CIs were wide, and equivalence could not be established. Interictal epileptiform discharges were visually unchanged. Intranasal DEX is an effective, well-tolerated sedative for pediatric EEG, and a weight-stratified dosing strategy appears practical. In a small paired subgroup, no significant spectral differences from chloral hydrate were detected; these preliminary quantitative findings warrant confirmation in larger studies.

papers.title: Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method versus CBT-I for Sleep-Onset Chronic Insomnia: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol Integrating fMRI and PSG.
papers.abstract: Sleep-onset chronic insomnia is one of the most common sleep disorders in clinical practice and carries a substantial multidimensional burden, including somatic symptoms, emotional distress, and impaired quality of life. Although Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method has long been used to promote sleep, its specific efficacy for this subtype lacks adequate empirical support. To assess the long-term efficacy and safety of PLWNT in sleep-onset chronic insomnia and to investigate, via multimodal techniques, its modulatory effects on cerebral cortical networks. This prospective, single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trial will enroll 128 patients with ICSD-3-diagnosed sleep-onset chronic insomnia, randomized 1:1 to a 12-week PLWNT or CBT-I intervention in a superiority design. The primary endpoint is the baseline-to-week-12 change in PSQI total score. Secondary measures include validated scales (ISI, PSAS, HADS, PSS, HAS, MEQ, MFI-20, GSRS, SF-36), sleep diary, actigraphy, blood biomarkers, gut microbiota, PSG, and resting-state fMRI. Exploratory mechanistic endpoints include (1) EEG-derived spectral power and wPLI within the DMN, SN, and CEN during wakefulness, sleep-onset latency, and sleep stages (N1-N3, REM), and (2) resting-state fMRI connectivity of the same networks. Clinical assessments occur at baseline (week 0), week 6, week 12 (end of intervention), and weeks 16, 20, 24, and 36 after randomization (7 time points); laboratory and imaging measures are obtained at baseline and week 12 only. Primary analysis will use generalized estimating equations on LOCF-imputed data, with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis. This randomized controlled trial directly compares PLWNT with CBT-I for sleep-onset chronic insomnia, integrating clinical outcome measures with neuroimaging-based mechanistic insights. The findings could position PLWNT as a non-drug therapeutic option backed by objective imaging data.

papers.title: From sleep complaints to clinical phenotypes: A tiered assessment and integrated management framework for sleep comorbidities in Epilepsy-A narrative review.
papers.abstract: Sleep disorders are among the most common but frequently underestimated comorbidities in patients with epilepsy, with major manifestations including insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, excessive daytime sleepiness, restless legs syndrome, and periodic limb movements of sleep. A complex bidirectional interaction exists between epilepsy and sleep disorders: sleep deprivation, disrupted sleep architecture, and sleep-disordered breathing may increase seizure susceptibility, whereas nocturnal seizures, interictal epileptiform discharges, antiseizure medications, and mood comorbidities may further impair sleep continuity and daytime alertness. Although mechanistic links and individual sleep disorders have received increasing attention, a practical outpatient pathway that connects sleep-related complaints with screening, phenotype recognition, objective testing, and subsequent intervention remains insufficiently defined. From a clinical phenotyping perspective, this review proposes a complaint-based framework for the identification, tiered assessment, and integrated management of sleep comorbidities in epilepsy. The framework translates common sleep complaints into major actionable phenotypes, including insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome/periodic limb movements of sleep, excessive daytime sleepiness, and overlap phenotypes, while incorporating life-course and syndrome-specific considerations for children and adolescents, young adults, middle-aged adults, patients with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, and older adults with epilepsy. This review organizes dispersed evidence on sleep and epilepsy into a clinically oriented conceptual framework linking complaint-based entry, tiered assessment, phenotype-specific intervention, and follow-up reassessment. The framework is intended to facilitate recognition and structured clinical reasoning, while its feasibility and effects on patient outcomes require prospective evaluation.

papers.title: Behavioural sleep quality and quantity and their associations with age, salivary cortisol and abnormal behaviours: A preliminary field study in racing thoroughbreds.
papers.abstract: Sleep plays a key role in both physical recovery and welfare. However, sleep patterns remain poorly documented in animals, particularly in athletic horses. This study aimed to provide a detailed description of sleep quantity and quality in training Thoroughbred racehorses and to investigate their relationships with age, abnormal behaviours, and cortisol. Thirteen Thoroughbreds (2-7 years old) were continuously monitored in their home environment for 48 hours. An ethogram was used to quantify sleep-related behaviours associated with the two main behavioural sleep states: non-rapid eye movement (NREM-like) and rapid eye movement (REM-like), as well as sleep interruptions (from day 1 at 12:00 to day 3 at 12:00). Sleep Quality Indices (SQIs), reflecting the relationship between sleep duration and sleep interruptions (SIs), were then calculated. Behavioural observations of four indicators of poor welfare (alertness, stereotypies, inactivity, aggressiveness towards humans) were performed using scan sampling, and salivary cortisol was measured each morning. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess the links between sleep quantity and quality, age, mean cortisol, and abnormal behaviours. Age was significantly associated with behavioural sleep quantity, being positively associated with total behavioural NREM-related sleep (Wald test: χ2 = 5.40, p = 0.02), and negatively associated with total behavioural REM-related sleep (Wald test: χ2 = 4.36, p = 0.04) and total recumbency duration (Wald test: χ2 = 5.68, p = 0.02). Morning cortisol concentrations were negatively associated with Total SQI (Wald test: χ2 = 5.26, p = 0.02) and Combined SQI (Wald test: χ2 = 5.60, p = 0.02). Likewise, horses displaying abnormal behaviours more frequently had lower Total SQI (Wald test: χ2 = 4.07, p = 0.04), pointing to a potential link between stress or altered welfare and poorer sleep quality. These findings suggest that, whilst the type and duration of equine behavioural-related sleep may be mainly affected by age, sleep quality is associated with both cortisol levels and the expression of abnormal behaviours, indicating that poor sleep quality may be linked to poor welfare in this population of horses. Overall, these findings highlight behavioural sleep quality as a potential component of racehorse welfare assessment and warrant further investigation into the factors influencing sleep in athletic horses.

papers.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging.
papers.abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2× and 2.25× compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16×. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258× speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. Evaluated across all 62 subjects in the public MASS-SS3 dataset using 31-fold leave-two-subject-out cross-validation, the mixed-precision approach with hybrid quantization maintains 5-class accuracy within 0.15% of the floating-point baseline when optimized for general sleep staging and N3 sensitivity within 0.51% when optimized for deep-sleep detection. The developed techniques are broadly applicable to EEG-based DL workloads.

papers.title: Non-coding RNAs in circadian network regulation and disease: from oscillatory coupling to precision chronomedicine.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms are sustained by a hierarchically organized transcription-translation feedback loop (TTFL) that coordinates physiological processes across tissues. Emerging evidence indicates that non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs, long non-coding RNAs, and circular RNAs, are integral components of this oscillatory system. Rather than functioning solely as downstream regulators, ncRNAs modulate core clock genes, mediate environmental entrainment, and couple central and peripheral oscillators to tissue-specific outputs. Disruption of ncRNA-clock interactions destabilizes oscillatory amplitude, alters phase coherence, and weakens network robustness, thereby contributing to metabolic disorders, neuropsychiatric diseases, inflammatory conditions, and tumor progression. Increasing experimental evidence from inducible genetic models and functional rescue studies supports a causal role for specific ncRNAs in circadian network destabilization rather than mere association. Beyond local regulation, circulating and exosomal ncRNAs may act as systemic time signals that coordinate inter-organ communication. This systems-level perspective reframes circadian dysfunction as a network instability state in which feedback perturbations propagate across hierarchical clock layers. Future progress will require temporally resolved multi-omics approaches, tissue-specific perturbation models, and chronotherapeutic strategies aimed at restoring oscillatory amplitude and synchronization. Integrating ncRNA biology with circadian systems modeling may facilitate precision chronomedicine and help determine whether temporal architecture can serve as a modifiable therapeutic target.

papers.title: Children become accurate years before they become fast: electroencephalography dates the separate maturation of decision components
papers.abstract: Perceptual decisions, a hallmark of cognitive development, become faster and more accurate from early childhood to adulthood, but whether the underlying components mature together, as a single global gain in processing speed would predict, or on separate timetables remains unclear. Behaviour alone cannot distinguish whether age-related improvement reflects clearer sensory encoding, more efficient evidence accumulation, fewer attention lapses or shorter non-decision processes, and prior direct measurements have typically come from small samples spanning limited age ranges. We analysed electroencephalography from 1,534 participants aged 5 to 21 years in the Healthy Brain Network during a contrast-change discrimination task. On the same trials, we measured the visual response and an evidence-accumulation signal, while a decision model estimated accumulation efficiency, attention lapses and non-decision time. We found that the visual response did not grow with age and retained 77% of its strength on missed targets. Instead, accuracy improved through fewer lapses and more efficient accumulation, both reaching half of their developmental change by about 9 years, whereas speed improved later: non-decision time shortened between 11 and 14 years and was longer in children whose accumulation signal rose later. These findings show that perceptual decision-making matures through dissociable stages rather than a single global increase in processing speed: mechanisms supporting accuracy mature in middle childhood, whereas those supporting the fastest responses continue to develop into early adolescence. This framework links developmental theories of processing speed to neural mechanisms of decision-making and provides a reference for identifying which component is disrupted in children who struggle.

papers.title: Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Epigenetic Changes and p16-Mediated Senescence in Vascular Dysfunction in Male Mice.
papers.abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a pervasive cardiovascular risk factor linked to accelerated aging. We investigated the underlying tissue-specific and systemic epigenetic mechanisms and the role of cellular senescence in the pathophysiology of OSA and associated cardiovascular disease (CVD). C57BL/6J male mice were exposed to intermittent hypoxia (IH) or room air (RA) (n=25 mice/group) for 7 to 210 days. DNA methylation profiling was conducted on left cardiac ventricle and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and the impact of IH duration was studied using regression models. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was calculated using a multi-tissue epigenetic clock. The role of p16-mediated senescence in IH-induced vascular dysfunction was assessed using transgenic mouse models (n=8 mice/group). IH exposures increased blood pressure and altered endothelial function in male mice. IH/RA differentially methylated positions (DMPs) were identified in left cardiac ventricle (n=5,747) and PBMCs (n=1,307), with minimal overlap (n=163, p=8.03 x 10-8). Both tissues differed in the EAA trajectory throughout the exposures. Epigenetic changes linked to cardiac dysfunction and cellular senescence, highlighting the Cdkn2a gene (encoding the p16 protein, a marker of cellular senescence). p16 expression was increased in aortic endothelial cells following IH. Systemic ablation of p16-expressing cells reversed IH-induced hypertension and restored coronary flow reserve. IH induces duration-dependent, tissue-specific epigenetic dysregulation and accelerated biological aging with p16-mediated cellular senescence as a primary driver. Targeting the senescent endothelium can revert OSA-induced vascular dysfunction, thereby establishing a novel mechanistic framework for cellular senescence as a therapeutic target in OSA.

papers.title: Circadian disruption worsens postseptic pulmonary fibrotic remodeling through a CLOCK/PIEZO1-linked myeloid immunometabolic program.
papers.abstract: Whether circadian rhythm disruption (CRD) promotes fibrotic remodeling after septic lung injury remains unclear. We tested whether CRD drives this process through macrophage CLOCK-PIEZO1 signaling. Lung specimens from patients with sepsis-associated lung injury and non-injured controls were analyzed alongside public murine lung transcriptomic datasets. Mice underwent cecal ligation and puncture or sham surgery and were maintained under stable or repeatedly shifted light-dark cycles; selected experiments included LysM-lineage Piezo1 deletion. Day-3 lung injury and day-28 fibrosis were assessed, and mechanisms were defined using genetic, biochemical and co-culture approaches. CRD suppressed CLOCK expression in macrophage-lineage cells, leading to increased PIEZO1 expression and aggravated collagen deposition. CLOCK repressed Piezo1 transcription through a promoter E-box. Loss of myeloid Clock reduced Clock mesor and amplitude by 66.3% and 90.3%, respectively, increased Piezo1 mesor by 54.0%, and produced genotype-by-rhythm interactions for both genes (P < 0.0001). PIEZO1 activation impaired lysosomal acid lipase (LAL)-dependent lipophagy and promoted ZDHHC19-mediated peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) palmitoylation and extracellular-trap formation. LysM-lineage Piezo1 deletion attenuated fibrosis. PIEZO1 inhibition or DNase I reduced epithelial injury and fibroblast activation induced by extracellular DNA-rich macrophage signals. CRD promotes post-septic fibrosis through a CLOCK-PIEZO1-linked macrophage immunometabolic program, identifying PIEZO1, extracellular DNA-rich traps and impaired lipid clearance as candidate targets.

papers.title: Association of Newer Glucose-Lowering Medications and Phenoconversion From REM Sleep Behaviour Disorder to Parkinsonian Disorders in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes.
papers.abstract: It has been estimated that as many as 90% of patients with isolated REM behaviour disorder (iRBD) develop an α-synucleinopathy, yet there are currently no treatments proven to prevent or to delay phenoconversion. This study evaluated the association between glucose-lowering drug classes and incident Parkinson's disease (PD), parkinsonism, and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) among older adults with RBD and type 2 diabetes (T2D). We conducted a target trial emulation using a retrospective active-comparator new-user design with 2016-2020 Medicare fee-for-service claims data amongst beneficiaries ≥ 66 years with RBD and T2D and atleast 12 months of continuous enrollment before treatment initiation. We identified initators of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2is). Patients with prior use of either drug during the 12-month baseline period or initiation of both drugs on the index date were excluded. Hazard ratios for incident PD, parkinsonism or DLB were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models with stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting. Hazard ratios were estimated using Cox proportional regression models with inverse probability of treatment weighting. A total of 148, 144 and 138 patients were included in the GLP-1RA versus DPP-4i, GLP-1RA versus SGLT-2i and SGLT-2i versus DPP-4i cohorts, respectively. Compared with DPP-4i use, GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower risk of PD (HR, 0.02; 95% CI, 0.001-0.20), parkinsonism (HR, 0.08; 95% CI, 0.01-0.96) and the PD or parkinsonism composite (HR, 0.11; 95% CI, 0.01-0.83), but not DLB (HR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.04-5.37). Similarly, compared with DPP-4i use, SGLT-2i use was associated with a lower risk of PD (HR, 0.03; 95% CI, 0.001-0.97), parkinsonism (HR, 0.02; 95% CI, 0.001-0.87), and their composite (HR, 0.02; 95% CI, 0.001-0.86), but not DLB (HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.17-5.17). No statistically significant differences were observed between GLP-1RA and SGLT-2i users. Amongst older adults with RBD and T2D, the risk of incident PD and parkinsonism differed by class of GLDs. Use of GLP-1RAs or SGLT-2is was associated with a lower risk of PD and parkinsonism compared with DPP-4is, while no significant differences were observed for DLB. No statistically significant differences were observed between GLP-1RAs and SGLT-2is. These findings warrant confirmation in studies with longer follow-up and larger sample sizes.

papers.title: Sex-Specific Circadian Dysregulation in the Choroid Plexus of a Nitroglycerin Rat Model of Chronic Migraine: An RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.abstract: Migraine patients show choroid plexus (CP) changes, impairing the blood-CSF barrier. The CP regulates circadian rhythms, but links between CP circadian genes and migraine are unexplored. This study examined changes in the CP circadian gene transcriptome in a chronic migraine rat model compared with controls to identify migraine-related pathways. Chronic migraine model: Sprague-Dawley rats (3 females, 3 males) received nitroglycerin (NTG) every other day for 9 days; controls (3 females, 3 males) got saline. CP from the 4th ventricle was collected 2 hours after the final injection for RNA-seq. Migraine Behavior: Von Frey hair tests on days 1, 5, and 9, pre- and 2 hours post-NTG/saline injection, assessed basal and NTG-induced pain thresholds. RNA-seq & Analysis: Differentially expressed genes (p < 0.05, fold change > 1) were identified. GO, KEGG, and Reactome enrichment analyses were performed to assess changes in circadian gene expression. The NTG group showed reduced basal and NTG-induced pain thresholds on days 1, 5, and 9. Females had a greater number of upregulated genes (MT2A, SLC7A11); males had upregulated ZBTB16 and S100A8. SLC7A11, SCG2, and GRIA1 showed inverse regulation (up in females, down in males). Circadian gene expression altered: 10 genes upregulated (e.g., SERPINE1, MAPK9, ATF4), 13 downregulated (e.g., PER2, DBP, EZH2). Sex-specific differences: females (FBXL12, GPR157), males (NKX2-1, ATF4, CLOCK). GO/KEGG analyses revealed significant enrichment of circadian rhythm-related pathways, insulin resistance, and inflammatory response processes, with sex-specific differences: females showed enrichment in HIF-1 signaling and hemoglobin-related pathways, while males exhibited enrichment in arachidonic acid and leukotriene production. CP transcriptomics in the rat migraine model revealed sex-specific gene regulation, with females upregulating antioxidant genes (MT2A, SLC7A11) and males upregulating inflammatory factors (ZBTB16, S100A8), alongside circadian disruption (e.g., SERPINE1 upregulated, PER2 downregulated). Pathway analyses indicate enriched circadian rhythms, HIF-1 signaling (females), inflammatory processes (males), lipid metabolism (PPARα), and heme signaling, highlighting sex-specific and circadian targets for migraine therapy.

papers.title: Sleep quality moderating the relationship between hearing loss and cognition in older adults: Implications for Alzheimer's disease risk.
papers.abstract: BackgroundHearing impairment and poor sleep quality are prevalent, modifiable risk factors for cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease (AD), but their combined influence on cognition remains unclear.ObjectiveTo examine whether sleep quality modifies the association between hearing impairment and cognitive performance in older adults.MethodsData were drawn from 122 older adults in the MedWalk study. Peripheral hearing (pure-tone average), speech-in-noise (SiN), sleep quality (PSQI), and cognition (CANTAB) were assessed. Generalized linear models tested whether sleep quality moderated associations between hearing and cognition, adjusting for age, sex, and education.ResultsSleep quality moderated these associations, with effects differing by hearing type and cognitive domain. Poorer sleep quality strengthened the association between peripheral hearing loss and associative learning, with greater total errors (Exp(β) = 1.005, p = 0.010) and lower first attempt accuracy (Exp(β) = 0.998, p = 0.021). Poorer sleep quality also strengthened the association between poorer SiN performance and increased spatial working memory errors (Exp(β) = 1.009, p = 0.004) and slower reaction times (Exp(β) = 1.002, p = 0.031). A threshold effect emerged, with poor sleep quality associated with worse associative learning in individuals with moderate-or-greater peripheral hearing loss. Final stratified analysis showed a 15 dB increase in hearing loss was associated with 38.6% more associative learning errors among poor sleepers (PSQI > 5).ConclusionsFindings suggest hearing and sleep quality interact to affect cognition in domain specific ways that are relevant to AD risk. Prospective studies are needed to identify if joint interventions can reduce AD risk.Trial RegistrationThis study was registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical trials Registry ACTRN12620000978965 (https://www.anzctr.org.au).

papers.title: Extreme delta brush as an ictal pattern in anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
papers.abstract: Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) encephalitis frequently presents with psychiatric symptoms, seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, and characteristic electroencephalographic (EEG) abnormalities including extreme delta brush (EDB). Differentiating epileptic from non-epileptic dyskinetic movements remains challenging, and the ictal versus interictal nature of EDB remains incompletely understood. In this case, a 22-year-old man developed neuropsychiatric symptoms progressing to hallucinations, confusion, abnormal speech, dyskinetic movements, and generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Brain MRI was unremarkable. Cerebrospinal fluid demonstrated positive anti-NMDAR antibodies. Continuous EEG initially showed diffuse slowing without correlation to dyskinetic movements of grimacing, jaw thrusting, and limb posturing. During treatment, abundant stereotyped episodes of facial pulling with rhythmic lip twitching emerged and were found on EEG to have an ictal correlate consistent with focal motor status epilepticus. Following reduction in ictal burden, EEG demonstrated a striking pattern of highly stereotyped right jaw movement and right arm internal rotation synchronized to complexes of midline beta-gamma activity overriding each delta wave peak, qualifying as a definite EDB pattern with clinical correlate to each EDB complex. Thus, in this case, EDB was an ictal pattern. This case illustrates the overlap between seizures and dyskinesias in anti-NMDAR encephalitis and highlights characteristic EEG findings including the EDB pattern. Unlike classic descriptions of EDB as a non-ictal EEG biomarker of severe anti-NMDAR encephalitis, this patient demonstrated clinical motor events time-locked to each EDB complex, supporting the possibility that EDB patterns represent ictal phenomena, at least in some cases such as this one. Continuous EEG monitoring is essential to distinguish electroclinical seizures from dyskinesias and may provide further insight into the potentially ictal significance of EDB.

papers.title: Analysis of nighttime heart rate variability during rapid eye movement and non-rapid eye movement in OSA.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a heterogeneous condition. However, many inconsistencies remain regarding the analysis of heart rate variability (HRV) and autonomic nervous system (ANS) function differences among patients with rapid eye movement (REM)-related OSA, nonrapid eye movement (NREM)-related OSA during different sleep periods. This retrospective study included 373 patients with OSA who completed polysomnography (PSG) at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University from May 2023 to February 2024. Patients were classified into REM-related OSA (REM-OSA), NREM-related OSA (NREM-OSA), and non-stage-specific OSA groups according to PSG. Clinical demographics, PSG parameters, and HRV indices were compared across the three groups. Multivariable regression models were constructed to examine the independent associations of AHI and OSA phenotype with HRV, adjusting for age, gender, BMI, and segment duration. A total of 373 OSA patients were included (120 REM-OSA, 90 NREM-OSA, and 163 non-stage-specific OSA). In female patients with mild-to-moderate OSA, no significant differences in HRV were observed across the three phenotypes. In male patients with mild-to-moderate OSA, the REM-OSA group exhibited lower LFnu and LF/HF and higher HFnu during N1 and N2 sleep compared with the other phenotypes. During REM sleep, the REM-OSA group showed higher SDNN than the NREM-OSA group. In patients with severe OSA, the non-stage-specific group showed lower SDNN, RMSSD, and pNN50 during REM sleep than the NREM-OSA group. Multivariate regression showed that AHI was significantly associated with frequency-domain HRV indices across all sleep stages. After adjusting for age, gender, BMI, and segment duration, the REM-OSA phenotype was independently associated with lower LFnu and LF/HF and higher HFnu during N1 and N2 sleep, but not during REM sleep (explaining 8.6%-24.7% of variance). The autonomic effects of REM-OSA are sex-dependent and severity-dependent. In male patients with mild-to-moderate OSA, the REM-OSA phenotype was associated with relative parasympathetic dominance during N1 and N2 sleep, but not during REM sleep. ANS function may not be the primary mechanism linking REM-OSA to cardiovascular risk, and the autonomic profile of REM-OSA is more nuanced than previously recognized.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation, Occupational Stress, and Work-related Determinants of Sleep Disturbance Among Practicing Physicians: A Cross-sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation and occupational stress are increasingly recognized as critical determinants of physician well-being, with potential implications for healthcare quality and patient safety. However, data on sleep patterns and their determinants among heterogeneous groups of practicing physicians remain limited. To assess sleep patterns, lifestyle characteristics, and work-related stressors among practicing physicians and to examine their interrelationships. This cross-sectional, survey-based study was conducted between January and March 2026 among practicing physicians using an anonymous, self-administered electronic questionnaire. A total of 627 physicians participated. Data collected included demographic and professional characteristics, work patterns, lifestyle behaviors, sleep-related parameters, and perceived stress. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data. Among 627 physicians, 54.1% reported sleeping ≤6 h per night, and 51.9% experienced sleep disturbance at least twice per week. Nearly one-third (28.3%) reported working more than 60 h per week. Stress negatively affected sleep in 48.5% of respondents. The most common contributors to sleep disruption were anxiety or stress (44.2%) and patient emergencies (31.9%), while key work-related stressors included poor work-life balance (40.5%), administrative burden (36.5%), and high patient load (32.5%). Despite these findings, most physicians reported low tobacco and alcohol use and moderate levels of physical activity. Sleep deprivation and sleep disturbance are highly prevalent among practicing physicians and are strongly associated with work-related stressors rather than lifestyle factors. These findings highlight the need for system-level interventions targeting workload, scheduling, and workplace stress to improve physician sleep health and overall well-being.

papers.title: De novo POLR2A p.(L1127F) variant presenting with neurodevelopmental regression and dystonia, with favorable response to low-dose dopamine therapy: a case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and variable intellectual and behavioral abnormalities (NEDHIB) is a rare autosomal-dominant condition caused by pathogenic POLR2A variants. It typically presents in infancy with hypotonia, developmental delay, and multisystem manifestations. Fewer than 40 patients have been reported worldwide, suggesting frequent misdiagnosis and underdiagnosis. To our knowledge, neurodevelopmental regression has not been documented in confirmed NEDHIB cases, and no standardized therapeutic regimens are established for clinical management. The patient presented with neonatal hypotonia and developmental delay. At 2 years and 4 months, she developed sleep-associated dystonia-like nodding and limb tremors that were initially suspected to represent epileptic seizures. By 3 years of age, she exhibited marked neurodevelopmental regression: loss of the ability to walk and sit independently, together with deterioration of language function. Electroencephalography (EEG) demonstrated background slowing accompanied by epileptiform discharges. Whole-exome sequencing identified a de novo heterozygous POLR2A variant c.3379C > T (p. L1127F), which confirmed the diagnosis of NEDHIB. Long-term rehabilitation training yielded only modest clinical benefits. After initiation of the dopamine agent levodopa-benserazide hydrochloride, marked improvements in motor and cognitive performance were observed, accompanied by the complete resolution of nodding episodes. With dose titration during follow-up, her clinical status remained stable without symptom relapse. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum associated with POLR2A-related NEDHIB and suggests that neurodevelopmental regression may occur within the phenotypic spectrum of this disorder. Our findings also highlight the potential benefit of low-dose dopamine therapy, offering novel insights into the clinical diagnosis, differential diagnosis, and therapeutic management of NEDHIB.

papers.title: Lion Tracks: Protocol for a Microlongitudinal Feasibility Study of Health Behaviors and Emotional Dynamics in Mother-Child Dyads.
papers.abstract: Adolescence is a critical developmental period during which physical activity, sleep, digital-media engagement, cognition, and emotional health become increasingly interconnected. However, reliance on retrospective self-report and low-frequency longitudinal designs limits understanding of how these domains relate within individuals and families in daily life. Few studies have integrated ecological momentary assessment (EMA), passive sensing, and wearable monitoring within mother-child dyads. Lion Tracks aims to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an integrated ambulatory monitoring protocol. Secondary exploratory aims are to characterize within-person, between-person, and dyadic temporal associations among health behaviors, physiological measures, cognition, and momentary anxiety. Lion Tracks is a prospective, observational, microlongitudinal feasibility study targeting 25 mother-child dyads (50 participants), with children aged 11-14 years. Participants complete baseline assessments, 4 weeks of ambulatory monitoring, and poststudy assessments. Garmin wearables monitor physical activity, sleep, heart rate, and heart rate variability. MetricWire (MetricWire, Inc) collects passive smartphone screen-on duration and timing and delivers repeated EMA of momentary affect, anxiety, context, and behaviors. Digital-media engagement characteristics are self-reported through EMA. Brief mobile cognitive testing assesses cognitive performance. A hybrid EMA design combines fixed, pseudorandom, and behavior-contingent assessments to capture daily experiences while limiting participant burden. Primary outcomes include recruitment, retention, acceptability, participant burden, wearable compliance, EMA completion, and data completeness. Descriptive statistics and CIs will summarize feasibility outcomes. Exploratory multilevel mixed-effects models will examine within-person and between-person associations, while time-lagged and cross-lagged analyses will explore temporal relationships and behavioral synchrony within dyads. The study received approval from The Pennsylvania State University Institutional Review Board (STUDY00027664). Recruitment is ongoing, with 7 mother-child dyads enrolled as of October 2026. Data collection is anticipated to conclude by June 1, 2027. Analyses will follow completion of data collection. Lion Tracks represents Phase 1 of a larger research program designed to progressively optimize ambulatory monitoring and subsequently incorporate mobile electroencephalography to examine neural correlates of daily behaviors, cognition, and emotional functioning. Findings will inform protocol refinement and assess the feasibility of a scalable, multimodal platform for future family-centered behavioral health research. DERR1-10.2196/107879.

papers.title: Suspected Functional Adrenal Insufficiency and Unmasking of Hashimoto's Thyroiditis: A Case for Diagnostic and Therapeutic Restraint.
papers.abstract: A man in his 30s presented with progressive weight loss, fatigue, anorexia, and low mood that developed over several weeks following international migration and transition to night shift work, the changes that disrupted his sleep-wake cycle and circadian rhythm. A low 8 am cortisol level (2.9 mcg/dL) with a borderline low ACTH concentration (7.4 pg/mL), negative anti-adrenal antibodies, normal electrolytes, and unremarkable adrenal imaging, suggestive of secondary adrenal insufficiency. Given his hemodynamic stability, empirical glucocorticoid therapy was deliberately deferred in favor of cessation of night shift work, sleep restoration, and nutritional rehabilitation, which resulted in complete clinical and biochemical resolution within weeks. At six months follow-up, a rising thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) level, strongly positive thyroid peroxidase antibodies, and a heterogeneous thyroid on ultrasound revealed previously unrecognized Hashimoto's thyroiditis, a finding consistent with cortisol inhibitory effect on TSH secretion during adrenal suppression. This case illustrates that circadian rhythm disruption from night shift work and migration can produce a reversible functional form of secondary adrenal insufficiency that may resolve without glucocorticoid replacement. It underscores the value of detailed occupational and sleep history in patients presenting with unexplained constitutional symptoms and highlights how cortisol-TSH interactions can transiently mask the co-existing autoimmune thyroid disease. Clinicians should consider a period of clinical reassessment before treating hemodynamically stable patients with long-term glucocorticoid therapy and should reassess thyroid function once adrenal function normalizes.

papers.title: Gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids in idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder and Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) is a prodromal stage of Parkinson's disease (PD). This study aimed to investigate whether gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) show consistent alterations in iRBD and PD with RBD patients. We enrolled 29 iRBD, 24 PD with RBD, 17 PD without RBD, and 18 normal controls (NC). Fecal microbiota composition was analyzed via 16S rRNA sequencing, and SCFA concentrations via gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Clinical symptoms were assessed using motor and non-motor scales, and Spearman correlation analysis was performed to explore interrelationships. Microbiota analysis revealed that, compared with NC, Bifidobacterium, Blautia_A, and Azospira_A were significantly enriched, whereas Agathobaculum, Clostridium_Q, Faecalibaculum, Photobacterium, Copromonas, UBA3402, Acetobacter, and Sutterella were reduced in both iRBD and PD with RBD groups. SCFA analysis showed significantly decreased fecal butyric acid and propionic acid levels in both groups versus NC. Correlation analysis demonstrated that in the iRBD group, Bifidobacterium positively correlated with RBD disease duration; butyric acid negatively correlated with NMSS and RBD-HK; propionic acid negatively correlated with NMSS, RBD-HK, and SCOPA-AUT. In the PD with RBD group, Bifidobacterium negatively correlated with SCOPA-AUT and positively with HAMD-17; butyric acid positively correlated with MDS-UPDRS III. iRBD and PD with RBD share similar gut dysbiosis and SCFA abnormalities. Elevated Bifidobacterium and decreased butyric acid and propionic acid are candidate markers for iRBD risk stratification, but correlation does not imply predictive ability. Their value in predicting progression to PD requires validation in longitudinal iRBD cohorts.

papers.title: Circadian orchestration of the cutaneous microenvironment and chronotherapeutic strategies in inflammatory skin diseases.
papers.abstract: The clinical course of inflammatory skin diseases-encompassing atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, and chronic spontaneous urticaria-frequently exhibits pronounced symptomatic rhythmicity, most classically manifested as the nocturnal exacerbation of pruritus. Although previous studies have progressively elucidated the circadian mechanisms governing both the epidermal barrier and local immunity that drive lesion evolution, contemporary clinical regimens for most targeted therapeutics and biologics have yet to incorporate administration timing as a key variable for optimizing efficacy. This review systematically delineates the dynamic interactive network between skin barrier function and the immune microenvironment under the regulation of the endogenous circadian clock. Building upon this mechanistic foundation, we examine how the timing of each major drug class-topical agents, conventional systemic drugs, oral small molecules and macromolecular biologics-could be aligned with the circadian peaks of the mediators they target, and we distinguish the components of this framework that are supported by clinical data from those that remain hypotheses. Ultimately, by conceptualizing chronotherapeutic strategies for precise intervention in local microenvironmental rhythms, this article aims to provide a testable framework for future chronotherapeutic research in inflammatory skin diseases.

papers.title: Deciphering mitochondrial dysfunction and circadian rhythm-related pathogenic patterns for the pathogenesis of Kawasaki Disease and corresponding nursing therapeutic enrichment: Evidence from machine learning-driven multi-omics and clinical validation.
papers.abstract: Kawasaki Disease (KD) is an acute, self-limited vasculitis of childhood, with its etiopathogenesis intricately tied to systemic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. Disruption of circadian rhythms and mitochondrial transport, 2 fundamental homeostatic systems, are increasingly recognized as independent contributors to vascular pathology. However, their integrated molecular crosstalk in KD remains completely uncharted. The primary objective was to identify and validate a mitochondrial transport andcircadian rhythm (MRC)-related molecular signature in KD. The secondary objectives were to resolve MRC-defined molecular subtypes, to nominate and characterize a candidate hub gene, to define its cellular distribution, and to prioritize candidate therapeutic compounds. First, Peripheral blood bulk transcriptomic datasets of KD patients were analyzed. GSE68004 was interrogated via Limma, GSVA, and WGCNA to isolate MRC-associated shared DEGs. Second, non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) and 3 machine learning algorithms (RF, Lasso and SVM-RFE) were deployed in GSE63881 for molecular subtype identification and diagnostic model construction, with independent diagnostic validation in integrated GSE73463 and GSE73462. Next, leveraging single-cell transcriptomic data from peripheral blood samples of KD patients (GSE24757), we resolved the spatiotemporal dissemination and functional evolution of the hub gene. In addition, deep learning-driven drug screening (DrugReflector) and molecular docking nominated a candidate compound in GSE18606. Finally, differential expression of the hub gene was validated using q-RT-PCR in clinical samples from KD patients. The integrated MRC-related signature robustly stratified KD patients into 2 distinct molecular subgroups. FNDC5 was identified as an NK-distributed and MRC-related pathogenic factor in KD. BRD-K10482608 was nominated as a computationally predicted candidate targeting FNDC5 for KD. This study provides the first pathway-anchored MRC-related signature in KD together with a validated framework for molecular stratification. FNDC5 is put forward as a prioritized, hypothesis-generating candidate of KD vasculopathy, and BRD-K10482608 as a computationally nominated starting point for future functional and nursing pharmacological testing.

papers.title: Changes in negative affect and resting-state EEG power following an EEG-derived generative reality art experience: a pilot pre-post study.
papers.abstract: Physiological signals are increasingly incorporated into personalized immersive media, but little is known about affective and neurophysiological changes when such signals are used as artistic material. This exploratory pilot study examined an electroencephalography (EEG)-derived generative virtual reality (VR) art experience in which participant-specific EEG signals were symbolically transformed into prompts for immersive visual environments. Thirty healthy university students completed the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule and resting-state EEG recordings before and after a single 5-min experience. EEG analyses examined log-transformed absolute alpha- and beta-band power across frontal, frontocentral, and central regions, with false discovery rate correction. Negative affect decreased from pre- to post-experience (mean change = -3.13, FDR-adjusted p = 0.004), whereas positive affect did not change significantly. Absolute beta-band power decreased across all three regions, and absolute alpha-band power decreased in the frontocentral and central regions (FDR-adjusted p values ≤0.022). Exploratory relative-power analyses showed no significant pre-post differences after correction for multiple comparisons. Frontal alpha asymmetry did not change significantly. Changes in EEG measures were not significantly associated with changes in affect after correction for multiple comparisons. The EEG findings therefore do not establish a neural mechanism for the reduction in negative affect. These findings indicate that the experience was associated with short-term changes in negative affect and resting-state spectral power. Because this pilot study used a single-group design, the findings do not establish causality or therapeutic efficacy. Instead, they provide an initial empirical basis for controlled research on physiological data as personalized material for immersive art and affective experience.

papers.title: The regenerative hexagon: six domains shaping musculoskeletal regenerative outcomes.
papers.abstract: The classical regenerative triad of scaffold, cells, and growth factors has guided musculoskeletal regenerative medicine for over two decades, yet outcome variability after orthobiologic treatment is not explained by preparation parameters alone. Contemporary regenerative biology already recognizes that host immunity, mechanics, and metabolism shape repair; what is less developed is a framework that integrates these dimensions for orthobiologic treatment and states their interactions in testable form. We propose an update of the triad concept rather than a replacement of it: a Regenerative Hexagon that retains the three construct components and adds three host-state domains that modify the response to them. These are the Systemic Host Environment, encompassing the gut-joint axis, sleep, medications, conditioning, metabolic status, and the pre-existing immune profile; Biomechanics and Mechanotransduction; and Cellular Energetics, defined as the energetic and redox state of resident and administered cells, which biophysical modalities are proposed to modify. Six short diagonals connect non-adjacent vertices, forming two interlocking triads that generate the Regenerative Star, and the framework is read as a sequence of states across the phases of repair rather than as a static configuration. The evidence for each component is graded with explicit criteria, and interactions demonstrated within a single experimental system are separated from those inferred from separate literatures. Convergent mechanisms are proposed: sleep fragmentation in healthy volunteers and dysbiosis-derived endotoxin in mechanistic studies both engage Toll-like receptor 4 signalling, and host metabolic burden was associated with orthobiologic response in a preparation-dependent manner. We hypothesize that the pillars interact multiplicatively rather than additively, a proposition not yet supported by a quantitative model and testable in factorial trials. The Regenerative Star is offered as a hypothesis-generating framework rather than a validated clinical instrument, reorienting inquiry from which preparation is superior toward in which host a given preparation performs.

papers.title: Atypical delusional misidentification with alternating impostors in a single body: a case report.
papers.abstract: Delusional misidentification syndromes (DMS), including Capgras and Fregoli syndromes, involve disturbances in identifying familiar individuals. Atypical presentations may challenge traditional classification and illuminate processes underlying familiarity and personal identity. A 42-year-old woman presented with persecutory and grandiose delusions alongside an unusual misidentification belief concerning her husband. Despite his unchanged physical appearance, she believed that different individuals alternately inhabited his body. She expressed complete conviction without insight, while remaining organised, fully oriented, and functionally independent. Neurological examination and routine laboratory and urine investigations were unremarkable. Neuroimaging, EEG, and formal neuropsychological assessment were not performed. Voluntary hospitalisation was offered but declined, and the patient was subsequently lost to follow-up. The presentation shares features with Capgras syndrome, through rejection of a familiar person as genuine, and Fregoli syndrome, through identity instability, but does not fully correspond to either. Unlike classical descriptions involving replacement or disguise, multiple identities were attributed to one physically unchanged familiar person. This may reflect a disturbed continuity of perceived personal identity rather than facial recognition alone. This case illustrates an atypical DMS presentation beyond traditional categorical definitions. Careful phenomenological characterisation of recognition, familiarity, and identity may help clarify atypical misidentification phenomena.

papers.title: Navigating the diagnostic challenges of maladaptive daydreaming: a case report of ego-syntonic and ego-dystonic obsessive fantasies with functional impairment in a 17-year-old.
papers.abstract: Maladaptive daydreaming (MD) is an emerging and insufficiently recognized clinical phenomenon characterized by immersive fantasy activity associated with functional impairment. Its overlap with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and schizophrenia spectrum conditions creates significant diagnostic uncertainty, particularly in adolescents. We report the case of a 17-year-old female presenting with intrusive celebrity-focused fantasies, sleep disturbance, behavioral regression, social withdrawal, and reduced self-care. She described co-existing ego-syntonic and ego-dystonic obsessive imagery with auditory-like pseudo-hallucinatory experiences. The Maladaptive Daydreaming Scale (MDS-16) score was 76%, consistent with probable MD. Extensive medical and neuroimaging investigations were unremarkable. Differential diagnoses included OCD, schizotypal traits, ASD, and schizophrenia prodrome. Initial treatment with fluoxetine was changed to quetiapine, alongside cognitive behavioral therapy, occupational therapy, structured behavioral strategies, and family psychoeducation. The patient demonstrated gradual improvement in distress, insight, sleep, and engagement, although intrusive fantasies persisted. This case highlights the complexity of distinguishing MD from other psychiatric conditions in adolescents and supports the value of a multidisciplinary, function-focused management approach. Early recognition may prevent misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment. Not applicable.

papers.title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Reversible Rapidly Progressive Dementia Associated With ASIA Syndrome Secondary to Silicone Implants.
papers.abstract: A 33-year-old woman with a medical history of polycystic ovary syndrome on combined oral contraceptive pills, insulin resistance, and bilateral silicone breast implants (SBIs) placed 10 years prior presented with a 2-month history of intermittent myoclonic jerks involving the head, trunk, and lower limbs; polyarthralgia; and cognitive and functional decline (compared with being previously independent in her activities of daily living). Family history was significant for epilepsy in her mother and 2 brothers. Neurologic examination revealed disorientation, significantly impaired short-term recall, visuospatial memory impairment, and a limited attention span. Her speech was characterized by frequent paraphasic errors and anomia; she also exhibited mild gait ataxia. Diagnostic studies ruled out common autoimmune diseases. Brain MRI and electroencephalography revealed no abnormalities, and CSF analysis was normal. Genetic testing for inherited prion disease and Huntington disease was negative, and serum and urinary copper levels were unremarkable. As part of a paraneoplastic workup, breast MRI revealed intracapsular rupture of both SBIs. The implants were surgically removed with complete capsulectomy. The patient's symptoms resolved completely by the seventh postoperative day. At the 6-month follow-up, she remained asymptomatic and had returned to her baseline functional status. Given the temporal association between implant rupture, explantation, and symptom resolution, the presentation was considered most consistent with a case of reversible rapidly progressive dementia secondary to the autoimmune/inflammatory syndrome induced by adjuvants.
